title: Magnus Stenbock (prisoner in Copenhagen) ↔ Peter Malmberg: cipher correspondence; key in Malmberg's papers
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Peter Malmbergs (Palmcreutz) arkiv, SE/RA/720725/~/E 4698 (key); letters in Ericsbergsarkivets autografsamling
folio_note: Key: "chiffernyckel mellan Magnus Stenbock och Malmberg för brevväxling under Stenbocks fångenskap"; letters: Ericsbergsarkivet autograph collection (not yet located item-level).
status: Catalogue (E 4698): key for the captivity correspondence; "brev från denna brevväxling finns i Ericsbergsarkivets autografsamling". DECODE R4101 (KB, Stenbock autografsamling 1713) is a different, decrypted item. Not in the repo. The 24 Oct Riksarkivet sweep found the key only in E 4698; the letters themselves are in the Ericsberg autograph collection. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): not blocked: Erlund's 1732 manuscript in the Riksarkivet (SE/RA/760004/42, IIIF R0000422, public domain) holds the key (Lit. F) and interlinear decipherments of the intercepted letters, the escape contract included. Stenbock's enciphered petition to Charles XII (pp. 697-707) is a different code, only partly glossed by Erlund; Dudout has rebuilt about a third of its values with certainty. See targets/stenbock1713/.
why: Stenbock's secret letters from Danish captivity (escape plans led to his close confinement in 1714); key and letters both survive.

title: Bazaine and Castelnau → Napoleon III, Mexico, French cipher cable of 373 cable words intercepted by Sheridan's telegrapher Charles A. Keefer, never deciphered
correspondents: Marshal François-Achille Bazaine and General Castelnau → Napoleon III (copy sent by Charles A. Keefer → Gen. U. S. Grant)
date: 3 Dec 1866 (copied at New Orleans c. 9-17 Dec 1866)
shelfmark: Keefer to Grant, New Orleans, 17 Dec 1866, William H. Seward Papers (University of Rochester), Library of Congress microcopy roll 98 (Weber, Masked Dispatches ch. 17 nn. 46, 60)
folio_note: 373 cable words of a French numeric code (groups like 2209 613 562 273 15 2214, Weber n. 46) copied by Keefer from the line; plain text of the same message printed by Georges Girard, La vie et les souvenirs du général Castelnau (Paris 1930), pp. 117-118
status: Weber (Masked Dispatches, 3rd ed. 2013, pp. 114-116 and n. 63): Keefer 'could not decipher it' and hoped for the plain text from a French newspaper; 'There is no evidence Keefer ever solved the French cipher.' The plain text was published in 1930, so the content is known; the French cipher system itself was never reconstructed. Not in the repo (known.py: Keefer, Bazaine no hits).
why: A rare surviving ciphertext of the French numeric diplomatic/army code at the end of the Mexican intervention, with a published plaintext: a known-plaintext rebuild of part of the code that could then read Keefer's other French intercepts of Dec 1866.

title: US minister at Vienna → Secretary of State, cable in the 1867 State Department code with the code letters run together, 'never deciphered'
correspondents: US minister at Vienna (Henry M. Watts 1868-69 or John Jay II 1869-75; unknown) → Secretary of State (Seward or Fish)
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Telegrams received by the Department of State (1867 code period; Entry 209 'State Department Telegrams 1867-1869' cited by Weber) or Despatches from US Ministers to Austria (M46); exact item not identified
status: John Haswell to Hamilton Fish, 8 Jul 1873 (Fish Papers reel 95, LC), quoted by Weber, Masked Dispatches pp. 106, 131: cables from Turkey (decoded by J. C. B. Davis after long labour), Paris and Vienna arrived as strings of connected code letters; 'the latter one was never deciphered'. The 1867 code (letters and groups of unequal length, telegraphers merged them) is known (Weber 1979 prints it). 27 Oct 2026 (targets/vienna1873/): attempted; closed unread. Weber, Masked Dispatches pp. 106, 131 (Haswell to Fish, 8 Jul 1873) gives no date, sender or archive item for the telegram; the full 1867 codebook was not found online. Needs NARA RG 59 telegrams / M46 and the Fish Papers reel 95.
why: A State Department cable that was never read in its own time; with the 1867 code known it is a segmentation problem, and it would show what the Vienna legation reported in the late Seward/early Fish years.

title: Nevers to Villeroy, Saint-Quentin
correspondents: Louis de Gonzague, duke of Nevers → Villeroy
status: Attempted 22 Sept 2026 (targets/nevers1595/): 17 runs, 753 signs transcribed; key not in fr. 3995 (no. 76 read in full: same sign family and design, other values; nos. 65, 66, 68-75 no fit); homophonic readings ruled out under six unit cuts by a solver that reads a matched control. A nomenclator; needs the key or the letter as sent to Villeroy. Tomokiyo (2019) lists it undeciphered.
why: Nevers commanding in Picardy in the Spanish war of 1595.
